name: Kara
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Extinct unclassified Ecuador language; Glottolog lists only Paz y Miño 1941 and Floyd 2022; essentially unattested, no phonology

new_statements.quote: Piguchí: acentuado en la sílaba final. Palabra aguda propia del idioma preincaico de la zona. La actual acentuación en la penúltima sílaba, Peguche, se debe sin lugar a dudas, a la influencia ejercida por el idioma quechua.
new_statements.translation: Piguchí: stressed on the final syllable. An oxytone word belonging to the pre-Inca language of the area. The present-day stress on the penultimate syllable, Peguche, is without any doubt due to the influence exerted by the Quechua language.
new_statements.citation: Caillavet, Chantal. 2000. Etnias del Norte: Etnohistoria e historia de Ecuador. Quito: Abya-Yala / Instituto Frances de Estudios Andinos / Casa de Velazquez (ISBN 9978-04-642-9).
new_statements.locator: Parte IV, cap. IV-3 'Genero y poder en la sociedad indigena: los testamentos de un matrimonio de caciques de Otavalo' (pp. 455-471), p. 470, nota 3 (note to the toponym 'Piguchi' in the 1609 testament of Don Alonso Maldonado, p. ~463)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (archive.org scanned of Caillavet 2000, Etnias del Norte; IFEA edition also on OpenEdition, https://books.openedition.org/ifea/2869, HTML open/freemium). At text line 22021, between running heads '...ECUADOR 469' (l. 21897) and '...471' (l. 22081), i.e. p. 470, in the 'Notas' of ch. IV.3 'Genero y poder en la sociedad indigena: los testamentos de un matrimonio de caciques de Otavalo', note 3 reads exactly: 'Piguchí: acentuado en la sílaba final. Palabra aguda propia del idioma preincaico de la zona. La actual acentuación en la penúltima sílaba, Peguche, se debe sin lugar a dudas, a la influencia ejercida por el idioma quechua.' The note is keyed to 'una estancia en el desaguadero de es…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accentual remark found: a native (pre-Inca, i.e. Cara/Otavalo-language) toponym carried final-syllable stress, and penultimate stress in its modern form is a later Quechua overlay. By implication (and consistent with the many Cara toponymic endings written with final accent: -quí, -bí/-pí, -chí, e.g. Cochasquí, Pomasquí, Tuntaquí, Cahuasquí), Cara words/place names were oxytone. This is an ethnohistorian's footnote about onomastic material, not a phonological description; the language itself is unattested beyond toponyms and personal names.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the note itself records that the modern Quechua-ised form Peguche has penultimate stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Applies to a colonial-era toponym (citation/orthographic form in a 1609 Spanish document); evidence base for the language is exclusively toponyms and anthroponyms, so 'word stress' here means the accentuation of recorded place names. No first-hand phonological description of Kara exists or can exist (extinct by 18th c., no texts).
new_statements.identity_note: Caillavet refers to 'el idioma preincaico de la zona' / 'la lengua otavalo' spoken from Quito to the Chota-Mira river, i.e. the Cara/Caranqui language = Glottolog kara1506 'Kara' (name after Paz y Mino 1941). Not to be confused with Cara (Teriya) of Nigeria (en-Wikipedia 'Cara language'). The statement concerns a single Otavalo-area toponym (Piguchi'/Peguche); the language is known only from toponyms and anthroponyms.

sources.note: Ch. IV-3 p. 470 n. 3: the toponym Piguchi' (modern Peguche, Otavalo) is stressed on the final syllable, 'palabra aguda propia del idioma preincaico de la zona'; the modern penultimate stress is attributed to Quechua influence. Ch. I-5 (Toponimia historica, pp. 103-107) discusses i/e, o/u and voicing variation in colonial spellings of the aboriginal language but nothing further on accent. Only accent remark in the book (full-text grep).
